transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-29
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Alice Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Singh (Redwood CSM), Javier Ortiz (Arcadia CTO), Maya Patel (Arcadia Head of ML), Samir Gupta (Arcadia DevOps), Lena Park (Arcadia Product), Rajesh Nair (Arcadia Finance)

Summary: Quick QBR and health check. Review of last quarter usage (tokens/embeddings), two reliability incidents in Oct, cost-growth concerns, and plan to pilot Dedicated capacity.

Topics: usage, costs, reliability, roadmap, pilot next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Alice Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alice from Redwood, with Marco and Priya, um, we're gonna run through a quick QBR, go over usage, cost, reliability, and then next steps. Javier, Maya, Samir, thanks for making time.
[00:18] Javier Ortiz: Hey Alice, yeah thanks. Quick note, Rajesh is on for the finance questions, and Lena will jump in on product roadmap items.
[00:28] Priya Singh: Great, we'll aim for ~45 minutes and call out any deep-dive items to follow up separately.
[00:35] Marco Alvarez: I have the usage and perf slides, we'll keep them high level then go to Dedicated pilot scoping.
[00:42] Maya Patel: Sounds good. Our main ask right now is clarity on cost per 1k tokens and whether Dedicated really gives us the predictable throughput we need for Peak traffic.
[00:55] Alice Chen: Right, good. Quick numbers: over the last quarter your hosted usage averaged 18M tokens/day with peak spikes to 55M on three occasions. Most of the cost increase came from chat generation and some heavy embedding runs for search re-indexing.
[01:15] Rajesh Nair: If I can jump in, is there a simple delta to show Hosted vs Dedicated on unit cost? Our CFO needs the delta for approvals.
[01:26] Alice Chen: Yes, we'll send a tailored pricing sheet. Roughly, Dedicated reduces unit cost by ~35-50% depending on concurrency and batching. But it depends on how much of your traffic can be batched and cached.
[01:41] Samir Gupta: We're curious about caching — you mentioned prefix caching earlier. How stateful is that with multiple models? We have a KV cache question.
[01:51] Marco Alvarez: Good question. The runtime supports KV cache and prefix caching; in Dedicated setups the cache lives local to the GPU pool and persists across requests for the same session. There is occasional mismatch in transcripts where it's called K V cache or K-V cache — but functionally it's a per-pod cache.
[02:09] Maya Patel: Okay, are there any risks with multi-tenant hosted cache versus Dedicated?
[02:14] Marco Alvarez: With hosted, we do cross-tenant isolation; cache is ephemeral and more conservative. Dedicated gives you persistent caching benefits and more aggressive batching. That contributes significantly to cost savings for repeated conversational contexts.
[02:28] Javier Ortiz: On reliability — we saw two incidents in October where latency spiked and one outage window of ~12 minutes. What was the root cause and has that been resolved?
[02:40] Priya Singh: I can summarize: one incident tied to an autoscaling misconfig where a model variant wasn't warmed; the other was a cloud provider networking blip affecting a region we rout into. We've implemented a routing fallback and warm-start policy and the incident postmortem shows the warm-start change reduced cold-start latency by ~40%.
[03:02] Marco Alvarez: And on the runtime side, we rolled a fix to kernel selection logic that reduced tail latencies for seq lengths > 1024. That was deployed in mid-November.
[03:12] Samir Gupta: Good to know. For the Dedicated pilot, what SLA and monitoring will we get? We need per-route latency SLOs and token-level cost breakdowns.
[03:23] Alice Chen: Dedicated comes with SLA options; we'll include baseline SLOs in the pricing doc. The Console exposes per-route metrics, token-level cost, tracing hooks, and logs. For Private deployments (VPC) you also get customer-managed logging options.
[03:38] Lena Park: From product, we want deterministic responses during peak sales events; can we do canary rollouts and automatic fallback to smaller models?
[03:47] Marco Alvarez: Yes, rollout policies are supported. You can set canary percentages and automatic fallback to a cheaper model variant if latency exceeds thresholds. That is part of the routing policy config.
[03:59] Maya Patel: On model compatibility, will our custom fine-tuned variant be supported on Dedicated without extra work?
[04:07] Marco Alvarez: Generally yes, but we'd do a quick model onboarding. For certain quantization profiles we may recommend a specific build; we'll flag any architecture mismatches during onboarding.
[04:18] Rajesh Nair: Back to costs — what's involved in the pricing commit? We have seasonal spikes; can we do burst capacity?
[04:26] Alice Chen: Yes, Dedicated has burst options. Commit levels affect baseline unit price; burst is billed separately but we can size burst buffer for your peaks. We'll propose a commitment that covers expected base traffic with headroom for bursts.
[04:40] Javier Ortiz: What about security — SOC2, SSO, KMS? We need documentation for procurement.
[04:46] Priya Singh: We'll share SOC 2 Type II, network diagrams, and our KMS integration notes. For VPC/Private we support customer KMS/HSM and SAML SSO. I'll attach redacted diagrams.
[04:58] Maya Patel: Excellent. Can we also run a performance benchmark using a subset of our production prompts to validate latency and cost savings?
[05:05] Marco Alvarez: Absolutely — we typically run a 48-72 hour benchmark with your prompts against hosted and Dedicated profiles. We'll need a sample prompt set and a baseline traffic shape.
[05:16] Samir Gupta: I can provide the prompt set and a replay script; we may need guidance on anonymization.
[05:22] Marco Alvarez: We'll provide a template; I'll own the benchmark doc.
[05:26] Alice Chen: To recap next steps — Alice will send updated Dedicated pricing; Priya will share SOC2 and network diagram; Marco will prepare benchmark plan; Samir will confirm pilot nodes and provide prompt set. We'll aim to start the pilot the week of 2026-12-06.
[05:45] Rajesh Nair: Timeline is tight but doable. Finance will review the pricing sheet.
[05:51] Javier Ortiz: Thanks everyone. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[05:55] Alice Chen: No blockers; we'll get docs out by Tuesday.
[05:59] Lena Park: One more ask — any roadmap features in the next quarter that would help us? For example more advanced quantization or model routing rules?
[06:08] Marco Alvarez: We have planned improvements in Optimize for automated quantization recommendations and more granular routing policies early next year; I'll share the roadmap brief.
[06:16] Maya Patel: Great. If there's nothing else, thanks — see you on the pilot kickoff.
[06:20] Alice Chen: Thanks all, appreciate it.

End of meeting.
